newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - ABARE cuts Australia commodity export forecast.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - ABARE cuts Australia commodity export forecast.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) on Tuesday further reduced its forecast value of Australian commodity exports in 1996/97 but said it still expects a rise over the previous year.
In its September quarter outlook, ABARE forecasts the 1996/97 value of total Australian commodities will rise 4.3 percent to A$59.72 billion from A$57.25 billion in 1995/96.

The latest 1996/97 export forecast is down from ABARE's June forecast of A$61.08 billion. The preliminary figure of A$57.25 billion for 1995/96 (June 30) commodity exports has also been reduced from the June estimate of A$57.35 billion.
ABARE's latest forecast for Australia's 1996/97 commodity exports is the second reduction in successive quarters.

In June, ABARE, the Australian government's main commodity forecasting agency, lowered its forecast for the value of 1996/97 commodity exports to A$61.08 billion from the March forecast of A$62.64 billion.
The value of rural exports, which make up about 40 percent of the total, is forecast to be largely unchanged at A$22.77 billion, against A$22.74 billion in 1995/96, ABARE said.
ABARE's latest forecast still sees minerals leading Australia's export performance.
"Although the export values of wool and dairy products are expected to rise, the export values of some major commodities such as wheat and beef are expected to decline," ABARE said.
In 1996/97, the value of mineral exports is forecast to rise by 7.1 percent to A$36.95 billion, ABARE said.
The major contributors to the forecast increase are greater coal exports, up by A$485 million, and crude oil, up by A$456 million.
In contrast, the value of gold exports is expected to decline reflecting a lower export volume after the sharp rise in 1995/96 when stock accumulations were run down.
Some easing in prices in Australian dollar terms is also expected, ABARE said.
ABARE's aggregate index of unit returns for Australian commodity exports is forecast to decline by 2.4 percent in 1996/97, after rising by almost five percent in 1995/96.
For rural exports, unit returns are forecast to decline by nearly 10 percent in 1996/97, reflecting easing world grains prices and weak beef prices, it said.

For mineral resources, unit export returns are expected to rise slightly as the effect of higher negotiated prices for the bulk commodities iron ore and coking coal outweighs the forecast lower average prices for a number of metals, it said.
ABARE said short-term economic growth in Australia was assumed to recover gradually, with public sector expenditure growth slow following tightened fiscal policy in the 1996/97 federal budget.
Strengthening private sector activity, supported by lower domestic interest rates, was expected to be the main contributor to growth, it said.
Headline inflation was assumed to decline to an annual average of 2.3 percent in 1996/97 from 4.2 percent in 1995/96.

"Considerable uncertainty remains about the short-term outlook for the Australian dollar, with financial market sentiment having a major influence on exchange rate movements," ABARE said. ABARE has assumed the Australian dollar will average about 77 U.S. cents in 1996/97 against 76 cents in 1995/96.
Interest rate differentials between Australia and major overseas economies are assumed to continue to narrow in the short-term, ABARE said.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
